title: Intercepting Routes
description: Open a modal without changing the URL background – intercept navigation to show overlay content.

slides.title: The Modal Dilemma 🪟
slides.content:
# Traditional Modal Problems

You want to open a login modal when clicking "Sign In", but you also want the modal to be shareable via URL (`/login`).

* If you use client‑side state, the URL doesn't change – no sharing, no back button.
* If you navigate to `/login`, the whole page changes – you lose the context behind the modal.

**Intercepting Routes** solve this by "intercepting" the navigation to `/login` and showing the modal on top of the existing page, while still updating the URL.

slides.title: The Intercepting Convention 📂
slides.content:
# `(.)` and `(..)` Folders

Use special folder names to intercept routes:

* `(.)folder` – intercept the same level.
* `(..)folder` – intercept one level up.
* `(..)(..)folder` – intercept two levels up.
* `(...)folder` – intercept from the root.

Example: In `app/feed/`, to intercept navigation to `app/photo/[id]`, create `app/feed/(..)photo/[id]/page.js`.

That page renders when you navigate from `/feed` to `/photo/123` – it becomes the modal.

slides.title: Intercepted Modal (app/feed/(..)photo/[id]/page.js)
slides.content: This page is shown as an overlay when navigating from /feed.

quizData.question: What does the folder `(..)photo` in `app/feed/(..)photo/page.js` mean?

options.text: It's a parallel route slot named photo

quizData.explanation: `(..)` means 'go up one level' from the current segment. So from `app/feed/`, it intercepts the `photo` route at the parent level.

slides.title: The Two Viewports 👁️👁️
slides.content:
# How Interception Works

You still need the actual `/photo/[id]` page for when a user navigates directly (or refreshes).

* `app/photo/[id]/page.js` – the full page view (when accessed directly).
* `app/feed/(..)photo/[id]/page.js` – the modal view (when intercepted from feed).

Next.js detects the navigation source and decides which page to render.

This gives you the best of both worlds: the modal pattern with real, shareable URLs.

slides.title: The Hard Link to the Full Page (app/feed/page.js)
slides.content: Normally, a `<Link>` to `/photo/1` from feed will trigger the intercepted route. To force the full page, you can add `target="_self"` or use a regular `<a>`.

quizData.question: What happens when a user refreshes the browser while viewing the modal (URL is /photo/1)?

options.text: The full page version of `/photo/1` renders, because there's no navigation source to intercept
The feed page loads with a broken modal

quizData.explanation: Interception only happens on client‑side navigation from a specific route. A hard refresh or direct URL access always renders the actual page.

slides.title: Modal Best Practice 💡
slides.content: Use a client component for the modal wrapper that calls `router.back()` on close. When the modal unmounts, the URL returns to the previous route. Also add a `default.js` file for unmatched parallel routes to avoid 404.
